chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Abd al-Rahman from Ala' from Muhammad from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a woman who had not performed Hajj, and she has a husband, and he refused to give her permission to perform Hajj, so her husband was absent; is she permitted to perform Hajj? He said: 'She is not required to obey him in the Hajj of Islam.'

key_terms.حَجَّةُ الْإِسْلاَمِ: The first obligatory Hajj performed by a Muslim

ai.seo_question: Can a woman perform her obligatory Hajj if her husband refuses to give her permission?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS), the concept of 'Taa'ah' (obedience) is specifically limited to the husband's right in the obligatory Hajj, distinguishing it from voluntary acts where his consent is typically required. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that the financial and logistical independence of the wife allows her to fulfill this pillar of Islam even against her husband's will, provided he is not physically preventing her departure. It underscores the priority of the divine obligation over marital authority in this specific context.
